newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mandela trims programme to rest.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela trims programme to rest.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela has trimmed his programme for the week ahead to rest before his second foreign trip in a month, a spokesman said on Thursday.

Concern rippled through the legislature in Cape Town when a note was posted on the gates of parliament saying that "due to unforeseen circumstances" Mandela would not address the new National Council of Provinces as scheduled.
Instead, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki cancelled a scheduled news conference in nearby Somerset West and drove to Cape Town to address the chamber three and a half hours later than planned.
Presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana said Mandela's programme had been rearranged to allow him two days of rest at his Johannesburg home this week and a limited schedule in Cape Town next week.
He said Mandela, 78, was in excellent health, but needed some time to rest and to spend with his family.
"We have rearranged the president's programme to take account of the fact that he has just returned from a gruelling four-nation visit to Southeast Asia," he said.
He said the decision not to address the Council of Provinces was taken separately in consultation with political leaders.
"The feeling is that he should address the council later in the year," he said.
Mankahlana said Mandela would leave on March 25 for a four-day visit to Bangladesh and India.

He said Mandela's main appointments next week would be meetings in Cape Town with Hillary Clinton, wife of U.S. President Bill Clinton, United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan and American comedian Bill Cosby.
Concern about Mandela's health triggered a dramatic slide in the value of the rand in February last year.
Mandela submitted to extensive medical checks and allowed his doctors to publish the results, which showed no sign of ill health, in order to allay market fears.
Since then he has undergone a minor operation to one knee to correct damage done during his 27 years in prison.
